source_span: The UST market is on a path to find the biting point where the level of sensitivity of AI issuance to yields picks up, or other parts of the economy break.
source_chain: This year's Treasury selloff is almost entirely real-rate driven (98bp of the 108bp 10Y rise), therefore AI capex demand for capital is the thing bidding yields up rather than inflation fear; AI borrowers don't slow down when funding costs rise 50-100bp because expected ROI runs in double digits, therefore the usual higher-rates-cure-higher-rates mechanism is broken and yields keep rising until a 'biting point' is reached: either AI issuance itself turns rate-sensitive, or another part of the economy breaks first (shown already in Russell-2000-vs-Nasdaq and S&P-ex-AI divergence, and in Oracle/Broadcom CDS and CCC spreads). Invalidation: a re-pricing lower of AI ROI expectations or a cyclical deterioration; CPI next week is flagged as the near-term trigger.
pulse_chain: 108bp rise in the 10-year, 98bp from real rates not inflation, therefore what's bidding against the government for that money is the AI buildout (SpaceX, Broadcom/OpenAI, Oracle financing; AI-ecosystem interest-rate risk issuance ~25% above Treasury issuance; Privorotsky: crowding out 'potentially immense'), therefore the question is at what yield AI borrowers start to care (Shah), and since a 50-100bp rise does little to slow AI borrowing against double-digit expected returns, the market is left hunting for the level where either AI issuance turns rate-sensitive or another part of the economy breaks first (shown in S&P-vs-S&P-ex-AI divergence and in Oracle/Broadcom CDS records, CCC spreads at a 3-year wide). Invalidation/trigger: next week's CPI print.
why: The lead theme reproduces Shah's 'biting point' mechanism step-for-step (real-rate-driven yields -> AI capex crowding out capital -> the either/or resolution of AI issuance turning rate-sensitive or something else breaking), keeps the same invalidation and CPI trigger, and attributes the framework and the crowding-out line correctly to Goldman's Shah and Privorotsky respectively.
